verdict.printed: Page 260 is a full-page engraving of the Flood allegory (a woman in a skin with a spade, a serpent, a man with a torch, a dark-skinned man, a three-headed dog, a chariot in the sky), with only small letter labels A–L and no title or text.
verdict.evidence: The English describes the engraving: 'In the center foreground (A), a woman stands prominently. She is draped in an animal skin and holds a heavy digging spade.' This matches the plate on page 260. It also adds a made-up glossary ('Key Symbols and Definitions': Allegory, Labor, Vice, Mythology), a title ('Hieroglyphics or Emblems of the Ancient Peoples'), a 'Romeyn de Hooghe' attribution, a summary and keywords. None of this is printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 75 (numbered 71) has only the header "ARMERIVS FLOS TERTIVS", a full-page woodcut of the plant with flower umbels, and signature E 4. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body, "A second species of Sweet William bears leaves around its jointed stems that are much wider... The Germans call it Steinnegele", translates the Latin on page 74 (numbered 70, "Altera Armeriorum species...", "Germani Steinnegele vocãt"). The title "THE THIRD SWEET WILLIAM FLOWER" and the picture description do render page 75's own header and image. The glosses and the added sentence about the third species on page 75 are not printed there.

verdict.printed: Page 35 (folio 16) is Hebrew commentary on Esther 1:19, with the verse heading 'אם על המלך טוב יצא דבר מלכות מלפניו…' and the comment 'אם על המלך טוב' below it.
verdict.evidence: The English 'If it be good to the King, let a royal word go out from him, and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media…' renders the verse heading printed on page 35. The English also renders the 'Bigthan and Teresh' commentary below it, which is on page 35. The closing summary and keywords are only metadata.

verdict.printed: Page 387 (header 'Morning Prayer', 1-24): the end of the Birkat Kohanim verses with direction glosses, the congregation's short prayers with acronyms, 'Adir bamarom', and the Etz Yosef, Dover Shalom and Iyun Tefillah commentaries.
verdict.evidence: 'by the hand of Moses, Your servant, [it is] spoken from the mouth of Aaron and his sons' and 'May the Lord bless you and protect you' are printed at the top of page 387. The 'Tree of Joseph' and 'Dover Shalom' sections also correspond to the commentary columns on page 387. The commentary renderings are loose and partly garbled with bracketed placeholders, but they come from page 387's own text.

verdict.printed: Nothing is printed on page 70. It is a blank leaf with faint mirror-image show-through of the INDEX LAPIDUM from page 69.
verdict.evidence: The English table (Magnet 22, Onyx 24, Schist 4, Moonstone 28, Emerald 30, Sapphire, etc.) renders page 69's printed index (Magnes 22, Onyx 24, Schistus, Selenites 28, Smaragdus 30). It also adds long explanatory notes, such as 'the lodestone. Highly prized for its magnetic properties' and 'in the ancient world, this name usually referred to Lapis Lazuli'. None of this is on page 70.

verdict.printed: Page 212 is a full-page plate with only 'Pag. 138.', 'Tab. LXXII.' and 'Tom. IV.', plus a botanical engraving of a leafy branch with flowers and berries. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body renders page 211's text: 'This is also a shrub-like tree, about a foot thick, bearing fragile branches...' and 'This is the large, hairy, five-veined Melastoma...' (both printed on page 211). The English also adds a long metadata note and several background glosses, such as 'Johannes Burman, the 18th century Dutch botanist', which are printed on none of the pages. The plate heading 'Plate 72' does render page 212's own 'Tab. LXXII'.

verdict.printed: Page 334 (header 'Ethnographie der'): the opening of the text on the monuments' ethnographic evidence (Samu, Neb-Amu), plus the end of the footnote on Herodotus' distances and the Ammon oasis, signed P. Ascherson.
verdict.evidence: "I now turn to the testimony of the monuments concerning the ethnographic conditions of the oases" and "Since we must in any case assign the fault of an error to Herodotus" are both printed on page 456. The English also adds a translator's note, a summary and keywords that are not printed on any page.

verdict.printed: Page 343 (numbered 323) prints the end of the sentence 'worden', Q33 'Bliebe er im Gehorsam?' with its answer, and Annotation 1 on Adam's covenant-breach and the serpent, breaking off mid-sentence.
verdict.evidence: The English starts with page 343's text ('Did he remain in obedience? No! The old serpent deceived...'). It then goes on with page 344's text ('2. I would wish that the Author had presented the nature of this breach...'). It continues past the end of page 344 into text printed on none of the three pages ('34. What was his sin then? ... like an unhinged clockwork').

verdict.printed: Page 269 (running head DEC. QVARTAE) has the second part of Valerius's speech. It says the matrons have often acted in public: Sabine women stopping the battle, Coriolanus's army turned back, the gold given to the Gauls, widows' money, and the Idaean Mother. It breaks off at 'nemo mira-'.
verdict.evidence: The English starts with 'I come now to that which is being discussed... the consul's speech was twofold', which is printed on page 270 ('Venio nunc ad id, de quo agitur'). It goes on through the Twelve Tables and the consuls Q. Fabius and T. Sempronius. None of page 269's content (Romulus, Sabines, Coriolanus, the Gauls, Idaean Mother) appears. The Hannibal, Cannae and Tarentum material is on none of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 347 is a full-page drawing of an Ionic entablature and architrave profiles with numeric measurement labels, under the running head 'LIVRE V. DE L'ARCHITECTVRE'.
verdict.evidence: 'To accompany the Ionic cornice described above... I have drawn and measured in Rome' is the body text printed on page 346 (page 169). The 'BOOK V. OF ARCHITECTURE' header and the diagram description do belong to page 347. The meta, summary and keywords are added commentary.

verdict.printed: Page 15 has the procedure (seven olive branches, whip, keep it secret), then the tin-leaf amulet with the BOR PHOR voces magicae and 'protect N.'
verdict.evidence: Page 15's 'Procedure: Take seven olive branches... Keep it secret; it is proven' and the amulet text are rendered. The English then adds page 14's content: the 'Greek Magical Papyri: IV.1227–64' intro and 'Hail, God of Abraham... Jesus the upright... drive away this unclean demon' (page 14). It also adds an invented meta paragraph about Osiris, Anubis and Thoth, plus many notes.

verdict.printed: A handwritten paper label on red cloth reading: नं० ५४४६—घ, सारसंग्रह : ज्योतिषम्, पत्राणि १५ (पञ्चदशानि), (संपूर्णम्). The three pages show the same image.
verdict.evidence: "No. 5446—D", "Compendium of Essentials: Astrology", "Folios: 15 (Fifteen)" and "( Complete )" all render the label on page -78. The added material is a closing paragraph ("This identification label acts as the 'title page'... likely intended for a student or a practicing astrologer") plus several explanatory notes, none of it printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 13 is six woodblock tree-foliage illustrations in a 2x3 grid. The only text is a cut-off fragment of the running title in the left margin. There are no captions or labels.
verdict.evidence: "Upward Mantis Style" and "Drooping Silk Style" with their explanatory notes, plus the "Number Eighteen" and "Mustard Seed Garden" margin notes, are not printed on pages 12, 13 or 14. They are composed commentary. Only the running title ("Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms... Volume Five") loosely matches the margin text, and the number "Six" does not match the "七" (seven) on page 14.

verdict.printed: Page 2 has only a small label reading "S.C. 28644" on marbled paper, with no other text.
verdict.evidence: "S.C. 28644" with a note explaining it as a Summary Catalogue shelfmark (page 2). The rest of the English describes the marbled paper and the craft behind it, which is a short picture description plus background. The Bodleian attribution and the paragraph on how marbling is made and what it was for are added background, not printed text.
verdict.note: The page 2 image shows the label and the marbled paper, so the body renders page 2 itself and nothing from the neighbouring pages.

verdict.printed: Engraved plate with 'P. 265.', the letters O.V. A.R. N.M. on the stone, and the caption 'Pressitque jacentes / Dulcis & alta quies placidaeque simillima morti. Virgil VI Aeneid.'
verdict.evidence: 'A sweet and deep rest, very similar to peaceful death. Virgil, Book VI of the Aeneid' is printed on page 316. The English also adds a long picture description, a glossary of terms (poppy, lion skin, lizard) with symbolism, a summary and keywords. It wrongly says the 'Pressitque jacentis' phrase is from Ovid's Metamorphoses. It also claims the catchword 'JA-' marks the start of the next page's text.
verdict.note: The body renders page 316's own caption and labels. The added gloss and commentary go beyond a short description of the picture.

verdict.printed: Page 698 is a handwritten page of Aramaic Zohar-style text: a main body, a narrow right-hand margin column and a block of lines at the bottom. It opens with names of rabbis, in the style of the adjacent Zohar pages. It contains no discussion of Maimonides, Ibn Ezra, the celestial spheres or the Intellect/Intelligible/Intelligent.
verdict.evidence: "the opinion of Maimonides (of blessed memory) in The Guide for the Perplexed (Part II, Chapter 2)" and "the Intellect, the Intelligible, and the Intelligent". Neither appears in the scan of 698, 697 or 699. The English follows the machine transcription of 698, which does not match the image. It is a Hebrew philosophical-kabbalistic essay composed for the page, not a rendering of any of the three scans.

verdict.printed: Page 272 (numbered 106, LIBER PRIMVS) has the end of the list of indignatio topics, from 'egeris; in eos, apud quos educatus sis' to the fifteenth topic, which breaks off at 'inimicis quoque et hosti-'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 272 in full, then goes on past its end with 'Conquestio est oratio auditorum misericordiam captans… The sixth is that through which it is shown that one is in misery beyond expectation…'. That text is printed on page 273, not 272.

verdict.printed: Greek text of Plutarch's Life of Eumenes, running header PLVTARCHI and page number 492. It runs from 'μέγα παρ' αὐτῷ' through sections IV and V and ends at 'Ἀντιπάτρῳ μὲν'.
verdict.evidence: 'great influence with him and took part in the council' and 'Alcetas, for his part, flatly refused the campaign' both render page 512's own lines. The English ends at 'toward Antipater', the last words printed on page 512.

verdict.printed: Page 254 (numbered 125, header LIBER II.) prints the end of the Deiotarus passage, then the argument against augury: Romulus's lituus, Attius Navius, the Etruscan boy, and the claim that the multitude is no authority, ending at 'plerique etiam summum bonum dicunt. num'.
verdict.evidence: Page 254's text is rendered in full, from 'and he saw both his enemy and his guest' to 'Most even call it the supreme good'. The English then goes on with 'Does the frequency of their opinion deter the Stoics...', the Ennius and Ajax left/right passage, 'Aemilia, the wife of Paulus' and 'restrain your tongues'. All of that is printed on page 255, as is the closing 'If someone happens to say something from their own affairs'.

verdict.printed: Page 124 (printed number 125) is the continuation of the Ivan Ilyich essay. It runs from "— теперь такъ" through the attempts to return to court, the pain "she" and the question "Неужели только она правда?", and ends at "невыра-".
verdict.evidence: The English opens with page 123's text ("tary, self-willed daring provokes indignation in people…", "He saw that the terrible, horrible act of his dying…"). Page 124's own text follows ("'It was like this—now it is like this'…", "is it possible that only *she* is the truth?"). It then runs into page 125's opening ("Or as Tolstoy describes a bit later… nothing to be done with").

verdict.printed: Nothing but a handwritten number 3268 on an otherwise blank page. The two neighbouring pages look identical.
verdict.evidence: The body says "An ink stamp of the archival collection department is visible" and describes "the 1900 Siddhanta Almanac" and "traditional system of keeping time and tracking planetary movements". None of this is on any of the three pages, which show only the number 3268. Only the number "3268" is faithful.

verdict.printed: Page 10 has only the title 漢武帝像 (Portrait of Emperor Wu of Han), the running header 三才圖會 人物二卷, the page number 五, and a woodcut portrait of a bearded man in a crown.
verdict.evidence: "Portrait of Emperor Wu of Han" and the header "Sancai Tuhui: Human Subjects, Volume 2 / Page 5" are printed on page 10. The bulleted sections on his reign (Confucianism, Xiongnu campaigns, Zhang Qian and the Silk Road, salt and iron monopolies, the Luntai edict) appear on no page. They are added encyclopedic background.

verdict.printed: Page 372 (Livy, Dec. III, header 'DEC. TERTIAE') runs from 'abiit. Per idem tempus Marcus Valerius Leuinus' through the Aetolian conferences and the treaty terms. It breaks off at 'Nauibus ne minus XX quinquerembus'. The margin has handwritten notes.
verdict.evidence: The first part renders page 372 ('Marcus Valerius Laevinus... came with an equipped fleet to the council of the Aetolians'). The English then goes on into page 373's text: 'Regarding cities, beginning from Aetolia as far as Corcyra...', 'Laevinus captured Zacynthus', and 'he captured the city of the Dardani'. That text is printed on page 373 only, after the catchword 'remibus'.

verdict.printed: Dense manuscript page of numeric astronomical computations with Sanskrit terms (shukra, ravi, vitribhalagna, yugānāsava, cara, lekhana, drgāsava, nati, sthityardha), with no title or heading.
verdict.evidence: "Venus 3388 3332 [Dha] 136 having multiplied 5230 15 the sidereal nonagesimal ... southern celestial latitude" renders page 477's opening lines. The added glosses (e.g. "[Dha]", "yāmya-śara; the angular distance...", the meta intro and the summary) are brief background, and the meta's mention of "the previous page" is also extra.

verdict.printed: Page 138 is the continuation of the astronomy chapter, running from 'elementatis contingentes' to 'Sic igitur mentes hominum futura'. It covers Alfarabius on the uncertainty of judicial astronomy, the dangers of the art, and the Policraticus and apostle citations.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 138 in full, then goes on past its end with page 139's text: 'the Most High gave the stars and planets as much vigor as He willed' and 'William, Chancellor of Paris... "If God did not wish it..."', ending 'It signifies' (page 139, catchword 'Signat').

verdict.printed: Page 512 (header PLVTARCHI, p. 492) prints the end of Eumenes ch. III, all of ch. IV, and ch. V up to Alcetas refusing the campaign, where it breaks off at 'Ἀντιπάτρῳ μὲν'.
verdict.evidence: The opening 'in his sight and participated in the council' renders page 512's first line. The English then runs past page 512's last words into 'ready to receive Craterus out of goodwill', and on through Neoptolemus' defeat and Eumenes' reply to the embassy, which are printed on page 513. The header 'EVMENES.' is page 513's, not 512's.

verdict.printed: Cover page with the title वाराही (बृहत्) संहिता, 'हिन्दी टीका सहित', and the publisher line खेमराज श्रीकृष्णदास प्रकाशन, बम्बई, on dark blue cloth with gold lettering.
verdict.evidence: 'The Varahi (Brihat) Samhita / With Hindi Commentary / Khemraj Shrikrishnadas Publishing / Bombay' renders the printed cover text. The added material is not printed on any of the pages: the note on the publisher's history, the term entries on Varahamihira's 6th-century encyclopedic work, the summary and the keywords. The three scans are identical covers.

verdict.printed: Page 295 prints "Fig. 299", a color plate of the god Lou-pan, the Chinese characters 魯班, and the caption "Lou-pan, patron des menuisiers. Intendant du ministère des Travaux publics du ciel."
verdict.evidence: "Lu Ban, patron of carpenters. Superintendent of the Ministry of Public Works of Heaven." (page 295 caption). The English also adds an unprinted background note: "Lu Ban, who lived from approximately 507 to 444 BC, was a famous Chinese engineer..."

verdict.printed: Page 688 has only the half-title 'THE LAWS.' with 'VOL. II.' and signature 'B'.
verdict.evidence: 'Library of Congress Cataloging in Publication Data ... Reprinted from the edition of 1804' is printed on page 687. 'THE WORKS OF PLATO, NAMELY, HIS FIFTY-FIVE DIALOGUES... IN FIVE VOLUMES' and the Proclus quotation are on none of the three pages. The English also adds a descriptive meta note and a summary. It does render 'VOL. II.', 'B' and '# THE LAWS.' from page 688.

verdict.printed: Page 55 is a title page with only the heading 'AVVERTENZA ALLA PRESENTE RACCOLTA.' and nothing else.
verdict.evidence: The body 'popular style when, in a simple tale or a rapid description where image chases image...' and 'We thus witness, with profound and reverent emotion, the intimate drama of Leonardo' is printed on page 54. The page 55 heading is rendered as 'NOTICE / REGARDING THE PRESENT COLLECTION.' The summary and keywords about Leonardo's prose style are also not on page 55.

verdict.printed: Pages 64-65 spread: Collars and Jewels of Past Provincial Officers, Grand Superintendents and Officers of Grand Chapter, with prices. Then the heading 'Information concerning various degrees of Masonry in England', on Mark Master Masons and the Knights of Rome and the Red Cross of Constantine.
verdict.evidence: 'The Sacred Pedestal is made in the form of a cube... S.K.I., H.K.T., H.A.B.' and the royal scepter/Zerubbabel passage are printed on none of pages -65, -64 or -63. The English is an invented entry about the scepter and pedestal that does not render the collar, jewel or degree text.

verdict.printed: Page 777 (header 'Commentarius in lib. XIIII.') carries the end of the Ep. XVI notes (Infimorum, Expedias, Leonidae, Kata miton, Xenon, Montanus) and the start of the Ep. XVII notes (In Cumano, In fortuna, His de rebus, Proficiam). It stops at 'a Caesare factum de' with the catchword 'Bu='.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 777 in full. It then goes on past 'might be confirmed' with 'To the great harm of the republic ... Philippic ... Capua', 'To L. Caesar', 'By the Kalends of June', 'The consul', 'Agamemnon', 'The sister's son', 'Appian lib. IV'. All of these are printed on page 778 (p. 384), not on page 777.

verdict.printed: A full-page woodcut of the Washing of the Feet inside an ornamental border. It has no text.
verdict.evidence: "The central scene depicts the Washing of the Feet, also known as the Mandatum" describes page 357's picture. The added material is the gloss "Latin for 'command'..." and the meta line tying it to Chapter 1's humility teaching.

verdict.printed: Page 579 (p. 131) is an alphabetical index page headed 'वर्णानुक्रमणिका'. It has three columns of Sanskrit headword—synonym entries running from विरूपी to विषमोहप्रशमनी.
verdict.evidence: 'Ugly — Porcupine / Virūpī refers to Jāhakaḥ' (first entry) through 'Strychnine Tree 422 / Vi…' (विषतिन्दुः, column 3) are all on page 579. The English stops partway through column 3, so the rest of the page is not rendered. The 'refers to' glosses and plant identifications are minor additions.

verdict.printed: Page 310 (Bull. 61): tables for Rhythm of Drum, Rhythmic Unit of Song, and Metric Unit of Voice (Tempo), continuing the Rhythmic Analysis of Songs of Dream Societies.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 410's drum, rhythmic unit and voice tempo tables, then adds page 409's tables: '### KEY ... Key of— A minor 1 109', 'PART OF MEASURE ON WHICH SONG BEGINS' and 'CHANGE OF TIME'. It also adds a meta line and a summary that are not printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 41 (printed 35): the end of the Avicenna quotation ("magis valet aurum..."), the closing remarks on the high price of gold, the Cap. VI heading and summary, and the opening paragraph of Cap. VI, which stops at "calculum suum alteri naturae potius,".
verdict.evidence: Page 41's text is rendered in full, from "gold is more valuable, and so it has been" to "they would have given their vote to another nature rather than to gold". The English then goes on with page 42's text: "in which, undoubtedly, they might find this thing which they most desired", the margin note "Gold a symbol of eternity", and "according to the will of that great Actor".

verdict.printed: Page 5 prints the dedication heading and address to Johannes Leisentrit, followed by the opening of the letter. The letter breaks off at the catchword 'Celebri-'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 5's heading and opening ('WHEN I HAD BEEN BROUGHT TO THESE REGIONS... greater admiration from the rest'). It then continues with page 6's text ('The argument for this fame of your name is greatly increased...' through 'I offer and consecrate the same... to the Reverend'), which is printed on page 6 (the next page).

verdict.printed: Running head 'Absinthium alpinum.' and page number 553, plus a full-page woodcut of the plant with roots, dissected leaves and a flowering top. There is no other text.
verdict.evidence: The title '# Alpine wormwood (original: "Absinthium alpinum")' renders the running head printed on page 630. The rest of the English describes the woodcut: 'branched fibrous roots at its base, lobed and dissected basal and stem leaves, and clustered corymbose flower heads'.

verdict.printed: Latin prose and verse on page 144 (printed folio 139, header PROSIMETRICUM) on the poor man as an image of Christ, Demetrius of Phalerum and Crates, and the philosopher fleeing riches. It ends with the couplet 'Divitias fugito...' and the catchword 'Cælum'.
verdict.evidence: "for the entire universe is a home to him, since he has no place of his own" is the opening of page 144 (nam totum universum ei pro domo est). The English ends with "Flee riches, a heavy burden to one loving heaven" (page 144). The added material is two short notes on Demetrius and Crates, plus a summary and keywords.

verdict.printed: Page 10 prints seven hall names (廣業堂, 崇志堂, 正義堂, 誠心堂, 修道堂, 率性堂, 彝倫堂) over a drawing of the rows of halls.
verdict.evidence: The English renders all seven labels, for example "Hall of Broad Achievement" (廣業堂) and "Hall of Moral Relations" (彝倫堂), all printed on page 10. The extra material is background commentary, such as "most advanced level of the Six Halls" and the emperor lecturing, plus a mention of the "Hall of Great Perfection" from page 9.

verdict.printed: Page 231 (numbered 112): Hebrew discourse on Chanukah, the eight days, Malchut, Pesach, the Milu'im, followed by a new section about Aharon, the Menorah and the name Ehyeh.
verdict.evidence: "Eight. It appears that the aspect of the stature is movement..." and "Aharon is the shepherd, he drew forth..." both match page 231's own text. The English adds only a short summary and a few glosses, such as "numerical value 161" and the "wings" note.
verdict.added_note: The summary and glosses are small additions.

verdict.printed: A pasted card with an emblem (pelican feeding its young on a rose-cross cube) encircled by 'PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA', and a handwritten 'A' in the corner.
verdict.evidence: "The phrase 'Hermetic Philosophy' ... is printed in a circle around the oval" and "HERMETIC PHILOSOPHY" (page -6); but it also adds a <term> definition of Hermes Trismegistus, a <summary> and <keywords> (about the 'Great Work', 18th century medicine) and a '1739 work by I.C. von Vanderbeeg' claim, none of which is printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 154 (printed 144, Perkins) covers Satan as a most powerful spirit and prince of the air. It says God limits his power by two bounds, and the first is his own created, finite nature.
verdict.evidence: "Both of these signs were observed in demoniacs in the time of Jesus Christ our Savior" and "Satan's malice and power are great" are printed on page 153. Nothing on page 154 is rendered. The English ends at "seeking whom he may devour" (1 Peter 5:8), which is also page 153.

verdict.printed: Page 51 has the title 護蓋圖 (Diagram of the protective cover). Below it is a drawing of a hat-shaped cover with a brim and a side tube. The margin reads 海國圖志 卷九十二 攻船水雷圖說.
verdict.evidence: "Illustrated Treatise on the Classics and Teachings... Constructing and Repairing Water Works" and "Well Protection" appear on no page. Page 51 is about 護蓋 (a cover) from the Haiguo Tuzhi's ship-attacking water-mine section. The English misreads the title as a well and invents a Jingxun Tuzhi water-works volume, with paragraphs of background. Only the title and 'Volume 9' are loosely and wrongly rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 818 (numbered 784) is a full-page woodcut of Staphis agria with the labels 'STAPHIS AGRIA' and 'Bißmüntz.' There is no body text. Only faint mirrored bleed-through shows.
verdict.evidence: The body begins "...so that the water retains no bitterness. It should be dried in the shade after being sliced and threaded onto a linen cord...". This is the Squill text printed on page 817 ("acrimoniam habeat aqua. Siccatur autem in umbra dissecta"). The labels are rendered, but the heading "THE HISTORY OF PLANTS, CHAPTER 300" and the "ABOUT STAVESACRE" catchword also come from page 817. The English also adds glosses and a meta note.

verdict.printed: Only a folio number '20' and a full-page illumination of a crowned winged woman and a dark figure in a landscape, with a floral border and animals. The left side is blank apart from bleed-through.
verdict.evidence: 'The Allegory of the Crowned Figure ... a winged female figure wearing a golden crown' describes the picture. It is followed by symbolic glosses such as 'a stag ... symbol of solitude, purity' and 'a darker animal, possibly a boar ... untamed aspects of nature', and by a note that the blank page 'suggests it serves as a visual meditation'. None of this is printed text. It is commentary composed for the page.

verdict.printed: Page 338 (numbered 336) opens by finishing the door-opening mechanism and the 'Nonnulli volunt' paragraph on Hero's Automata. It then gives the heading Pragmatia IV, 'Rotae versatiles aquam lustrationi necessariam fundunt', and the Clement/Hero text. A wheel and vessel engraving follows, with a margin note and the start of the construction.
verdict.evidence: "Some desire that, with the door open, various monsters of the gods and dances... " and "Versatile wheels pour the water necessary for lustration" are both printed on page 338. The opening lines (valves opened, the situla, the pulley weight) are not rendered. The English also adds a short gloss, "ritual purification".

verdict.printed: Page 46 is a blank tan sheet with no text, labels or drawings.
verdict.evidence: ".a. of . motions . of . which . the other . through . the . plane" and "I . of . wanting . to see . d . s . f . m" render the mirror-script notes printed on page 45. Page 46 is blank. The added summary, keywords and notes on impetus are commentary.

verdict.printed: Page 168 (header 'Tres Discursus initiales'): the end of the previous paragraph, then 'Pergit Sohar' with the Aramaic text and the Latin §§15-20 (Eleazar and Schimeon, Elijah at the seashore), then the start of the 'Commentarius Lorjensis' §11, which breaks off at 'nam fundamen-'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 1906's own text, including 'Rabbi Eleazar fell silent' and §§15-20. After the §11 start it runs on into page 1907's text: 'Since from this, souls fly forth, as is known... The second reason is this: that stars... were created through the grade of Wisdom'. That text is printed on page 169, so it is an added paragraph.

verdict.printed: Page 13 prints the title 正面圖 and a front-view figure of a child with labelled acupoints (百會, 神庭, 天突, 中脘, 氣海, 關元, 合谷, 三陰交, 內庭, 行間, 大敦 and others).
verdict.evidence: "Frontal View Diagram" and "Hundred Convergences ... is located at the vertex" render the 正面圖 title and the 百會 label, both printed on page 13. The added Conception Vessel and Acupuncture glosses, the meta text and the summary are extra background, not printed text.

verdict.printed: Page 131 prints the continuation of the lunar-eclipse commentary (secondary light and shadow, the Almias eclipse and refracted rays, universal and partial eclipses), the diagram with letters a–k, and the start of 'Cum autem fuerit luna' at the foot.
verdict.evidence: "Note thirdly, that it may seem to some that the moon can be eclipsed not because of the earth's shadow" and "let us describe the earth's shadow a b c d" both match page 131's printed text. The English adds only short bracketed <gloss>/<note> insertions.

verdict.printed: Page 27 prints only the running margin title 三才圖會 / 器用五卷 / 十二 (Sancai Tuhui, Implements and Utensils, Volume 5, page 12). Its picture is the right half of a carriage woodcut with canopy, wheel, banners and streamers.
verdict.evidence: "Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms: Implements and Utensils, Volume 5 / Page 12" renders page 27's margin text. The heading "Elephant Carriage (Xiang Lu)" and "The Lotus-Shaped Shaft Stands" come from page 26, where the caption 象輅 and the lotus stands are printed. Passages such as "celestial motifs" and "journeys to the Imperial Ancestral Temple" are composed background that appears on no page.

verdict.printed: Page 299 (scan 599): Hebrew discourse on teacher and student, the intellect (sechel) and the maskil, the light of the sun, ending with the catchword 'ובזה'.
verdict.evidence: "It is like if the student is not there, the teacher descends himself... until the intellect of the student returns to the intellect" and ends "And in this" (page 599). The only additions are short bracketed glosses and notes such as the Yesod and Chesed notes.

verdict.printed: Page 102 (numbered 45) has the sutra fragment 'शेषार्धगुणकयोगो रूपविहीनः क्रयो भवति', then the continued upapatti algebra showing the profit ला = (वि.शे−१)/स is the same for all, ending 'अतो वि मानं तथा कल्प्यं यथा (वि.शे−१)/स इदमभिन्नमथ च'.
verdict.evidence: The English 'Profit = (Sale·Remainder − 1)/Base ... This measure of profit is the same everywhere' renders the equations and 'इदं लाभमानं सर्वत्र समानमेव' on page 102. The added parts are the meta and summary paragraphs, the vocabulary margin and the glosses, which are minor. The English also renders the variable याः as 'X' and the symbols loosely.

verdict.printed: Nothing. Page 4 is a blank cream leaf with paper fibres and specks. Pages 3 and 5 are blank too.
verdict.evidence: "[This page is a blank leaf]" matches the blank page 4. The added background ("common feature in historical manuscripts", what scholars value) is generic gloss. The meta line about a "symbolic frontispiece featuring the Rose Cross and the Pelican" matches nothing on pages 3-5.

verdict.printed: Nothing is printed on page 6. It is a photograph of the closed book's fore-edge, showing aged page edges between strips of red-brown leather binding.
verdict.evidence: The note "A vertical photograph shows the fore-edge of the closed manuscript... dark reddish-brown leather" (page 6) describes the picture. The added material is the heading "Book of Chess, Its Problems, and Its Subtleties", which is not on page 6, plus the meta, summary, keywords and glossary, which discuss the "1257 volume" and "13th-century manuscript" and are not on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 312 (scan 318): running head 'THE WORKS OF HIPPOCRATES.' and a short text, the end of a summary ('both by others and himself. Extension... fracture of radius, of cubitus, &c.') plus the editor's note 'This treatise could scarcely be read without benefit...—Ed.'. The rest of the page is blank, with faint mirror-image bleed-through.
verdict.evidence: The English renders the page's own text ('Stretching the limb, if not previously performed, is to be carefully avoided on the third and fourth day'). It then adds an 'ON FRACTURES' heading, a table of Fœsius/Haller/Gardeil references and a paragraph beginning 'This is an admirable work by a wise and experienced man (says Haller)'. None of that is printed on page 318. It appears on the neighbouring page 317, or comes from the reverse-side bleed-through.

verdict.printed: Three captioned woodcut illustrations: 束帶 (girdle), 襪 (stocking), 舄 (shoe). The page has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The headings "Ceremonial Girdle", "Ritual Stockings" and "Double-Soled Ritual Shoes" match the three captions printed on page 46. The notes under them add material that is on no page. Examples are "typically made of red silk" and "designed to elevate the wearer above the damp ground of an outdoor altar". The opening meta paragraph also refers to an inventory that continues from earlier pages.
verdict.note: Page 46 prints only the three captions and their pictures. The English renders those captions. It then adds long invented notes on materials, function, and rank symbolism that are printed nowhere.

verdict.printed: Page 291 is a plate: Pag. 208, Tab. LXXX, Tom. VI, Fig. 1, 2 and 3 labels, and an engraving of a sea fan and two branching marine shrubs. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: "The fifth species is an ash-colored, woody, and brittle shrub. It stands one and a half feet high..." This is the Chapter 6 Sea Hay text printed on page 290. The plate labels (Plate 80, Volume 6, Figures 1-3) are rendered, but the body is page 290's text.

verdict.printed: Page 938 is blank apart from faint, mirrored show-through of the reverse side. It reads as a short French and German 'Avis au Relieur' / 'Bericht an den Buchbinder' (binder's notice about placing the plates), above which are faint lines of a list.
verdict.evidence: 'NOTICE TO THE READER ... The Editor gives notice ... figures arranged in width' loosely renders the faint show-through notice on page 938. The 1724 Huygens framing in the meta, summary and keywords is not printed on any of the three pages, and 'Reader' is probably a mistranslation of 'Relieur' (binder).

verdict.printed: Page 18 is a mirrored, faded scan of the preface's next page, with a few lines of printed preface text and small marginal notes. It is barely legible.
verdict.evidence: "QUESTION", page number "41", and "possibly of a theological or philosophical nature" appear on none of the three pages. The English is an invented placeholder, not a rendering of the preface text.

verdict.printed: Running head 'INTRODUCTIO IN' and a woodcut of a palm with six Latin line labels (Linea mesal. fortune, Linea vite uel cord., media nat., L. epatis fo., Percussio man., Restricta mulieris). Faint show-through of text from the other side of the leaf.
verdict.evidence: "The table line of fortune", "The line of life, or of the heart" and "The wrist-lines of the woman" render page 18's own labels. The added material is short glosses on each label, plus a meta sentence about page 17.

verdict.printed: Page 144 (printed p. 139) begins 'nam totum universum ei pro domo est' and continues with the poor man as Christ's companion, Demetrius and Crates, and the verses on fleeing riches.
verdict.evidence: 'placing his merchandise into a single ship... Solomon: The poor man is worthier, and sufficient to himself' is the printed text of page 143 (printed p. 138). Nothing from 'nam totum universum ei pro domo est' on page 144 is rendered. The added summary is a minor addition.

verdict.printed: Page 546 (462) has the end of the Sanskrit commentary on the bhuja: the gnomon base is summed or differenced with agra, and the true bhuja is found with a worked example of 140 and 90 minutes. Below it are the Hindi Bhashabhashya and the start of the Upapatti.
verdict.evidence: "Suppose the Moon's side is 140 north. The Sun's side is 90 Kalas... leaves a true side of 50 minutes" and "Commentary in the Common Tongue" are both printed on page 546. The meta and summary lines are short added description.

verdict.printed: Page 853 (numbered 772) is Cap. LXVII, items 16–21 on court emblems, the heading 'Emblemata de eadem materia', and the start of section XXII. The text breaks off mid-sentence at 'supplex pulloque in habitu'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 853's items 16–21 and the XXII opening, then carries on past the page break: 'the King turned to his brother... two chests... gilded... stench of corpses', the bagpiper, tobacco and smoke emblems, and 'But I conclude...'. This is printed on page 854, not 853. The final summary and keywords are also not printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 154 (printed 144, header Gvilielmi Perkinsi): Satan's great power (prince of the air, God of this world), the two limits God sets on it, and the first limit, his finite created nature.
verdict.evidence: "For he is called the prince who has power over the air, and the God of this world" and "The first is his own nature, through which he is a creature, and therefore finite" (both on page 154). The only addition is a short summary and keyword list after the body.

verdict.printed: Cover label reading 'बृहत्पाराशरहोरा-शास्त्रम्' in a decorative border on a red cloth cover, with the CC-0 Shri Krishna Museum / eGangotri watermark. The three scans are identical.
verdict.evidence: 'THE GREAT PARASHARA ASTROLOGY-TREATISE.' translates the label title. The added material is background glosses, such as the dialogue between Parashara and Maitreya and Jyotisha as a Vedanga, plus a '19th or early 20th-century' dating.

verdict.printed: Page 646 is a handwritten cursive page. It opens with a line beginning ס' ("I said I will climb the palm tree" with a commentary note), followed by Psalm 128, Psalm 23 and the start of Psalm 90, separated by rules.
verdict.evidence: "Happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in His ways..." and "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want" both render page 646's own text. The added meta line and the summary naming "daily devotion" are minor extras. I could not read the cursive fully, so this relies partly on the transcription.

verdict.printed: No text, only a blank stained coarse cloth/jute cover, apart from a small digitization credit line (CC-0 Shri Krishna Museum, Kurukshetra, Digitized by eGangotri).
verdict.evidence: "The surface of this page consists of a coarse-woven fabric, likely a heavy linen or jute" describes the cloth on page -383. The added background is "This type of 'limp binding' was common for practical notebooks or archival records that did not require the expense of leather or wooden boards."

verdict.printed: Page 34 has eight lines of Sanskrit verse. They cover cooking gandhaka in mustard oil with the pishtika, the trikatu, vacha, musta, vidanga, chitraka and visha mixture with pathya, the gunja dose, the Sankocha pishtika for prasutivata and kushtha, and a second pill recipe with ajamutra. There is a margin number 15 and a catchword.
verdict.evidence: "cook two palas of gandhaka in katutaila" and "grind these together with ajamutra... form them into pills" render page 34's lines. The extras are inline glosses plus a short summary and keywords.

verdict.printed: Page 116 has the numeral XXV, a full-page engraving of a woman with a lamp searching a canopied bed while a winged child sleeps on the floor, and the Latin caption from Cantic. 3 (In lectulo meo...).
verdict.evidence: "Why do you seek in bed / Your Spouse, indiscreet Lover?" is the French poem printed on page 115. Only the Song of Solomon caption and the picture description come from page 116. The added meta, notes and summary are glosses.

verdict.printed: Spread 856-857: Assertio on Divine free volition, §76 against Bannes, his corollaries on the indifference of judgment as the root of liberty, and the start of §77.
verdict.evidence: "This is against Bannes in Part 1, Question 19, Article 10" and "the new Sun of this doctrine" are both printed on this spread (856-857). The added glosses (Bañez, Thomist) are brief.

verdict.printed: Page 378: the argument of Ep. 6 and Cicero's letter to Varro (Caninius, Caesar's arrival, Alsium or Ostia, the civil war, Varro's studies at Tusculum). The text is in two columns and breaks off mid-word at 'qui n'.
verdict.evidence: The letter, argument and heading render page 454's text. The English then adds an 'E X P L A N A T I O' section ('Adventus: Of Caesar from Africa... Naevius in the Tarentilla, according to Carisius') and a closing ('I will therefore do what I was asked... Farewell'). Neither is printed on page 454, where the letter cuts off at 'qui n'. Only fragments of the Utrubique discussion appear in page 455's commentary.

verdict.printed: Page 583 (Liber Quartus): Latin text on a planet's magnetic fibres turning toward the Sun, with the magnetic compass-box example and a diagram of a castle with four compass boxes.
verdict.evidence: The English says "heavily annotated manuscript page where the primary marginalia is currently illegible" and lists 60+ "Illegible" margin notes. None of this is printed on page 615, 614 or 616. It is a description composed about the transcription's artefacts, and the real body text is not rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 206 (p. 69, LIB. IIII.) prints the end of the Latin discussion of -osus adjectives (vinosus, formosus, facundiosa), the chapter heading for Book 4 ch. X, and only the first two lines of the chapter ('Ante legem... Alias primus rogabatur, qui a CENS.').
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 206's text, then continues with 'Gaius Caesar, in the consulship which he held with Marcus Bibulus...' and 'Cato... the Senate stood up and followed Cato to the prison', plus the final line 'What and of what kind are those things which Aristoxenus committed to memory'. All of that is printed on page 207, not 206. Bracketed notes such as 'meaning: he filibustered to prevent a vote' are minor additions.

verdict.printed: Page 89 is a landscape picture. Its title reads 雪竇圖 with 四明附 beside it, and it carries a few small labels, including 石夫人, 唐妙名山 and what looks like 舍利林.
verdict.evidence: "Illustration of Xuedou Mountain / Attached to Siming Mountain" renders the title on page 89. The long notes on "Bell Frame Rocks", "Flower Peak Mountain", "Deer Park" and "Thousand-Foot Cliff" are composed background. Those labels are not clearly printed on the page, and 石夫人 is not rendered.
